new_statements.rule_in_words: No rule. Thelwall states only that the Daju languages he recorded (Sila, Nyala, Lagowa, Shatt, Liguri) are not tonal and that the vowel duration he transcribed may reflect stressed syllables; position of stress is not stated. Baygo/Bego was not in his corpus and no source gives any stress information for it.
new_statements.domain_note: Group-level remark about five Daju languages other than Bego; the only Baygo materials (MacMichael 1920/1922 and Santandrea 1948 wordlists) say nothing about stress, accent or tone. Not a Baygo statement and not usable for the catalog as one.
new_statements.identity_note: Baygo = Bego/Beigo/Beygo/Bayko (self-name Beoge), a section of Nyala (Darfur) Daju per Stevenson/Thelwall; closest described relative is Dar Fur Daju darf1239 (Nyala, Lagowa). Thelwall's stress remark covers Dar Sila Daju dars1235, Dar Fur Daju darf1239 (Nyala, Lagowa), Shatt shat1244 and Logorik/Liguri logo1261, not bayg1239.

sources.note: Sect. 3 Systematic phonetics (pp. 172-173), covering his five languages Sila, Nyala, Lagowa, Shatt, Liguri: 'No vowel length opposition has been established for any language. Since these languages are not tonal this may well indicate my perception of stressed syllables.' Bego is listed as a section of the group (p. 167) but was not in his corpus; he names MacMichael 1920 and Santandrea 1948 as the only Bego vocabularies (p. 168). No stress rule given.
